text:
maya: FYI ran a focused bench on the mixed FP8/INT4 path with per-layer exclusions (embed + lm_head excluded). results look weird, need eyes.

alex: can you paste the exact config you used? especially kernel_selector flags and batch sizes.

maya: config: `--quant=per_layer --exclude_layers=embed,lm_head --kernels=fp8,int4 --batch=8 --kv_cache=on --calib=on`

sam: quick question — calib=on means we run the online calibration stage before canary, right? that step shouldn't be in the hot loop.

maya: correct, we run a 1k-step calibration per model before collecting perf numbers. but I noticed a 12-18% tail latency increase when KV cache warm is used.

rachel: do you have flamegraphs or perf traces? could be kernel dispatch jitter when switching quantized vs fp kernels for some layers.

maya: attaching short snippet from perf-bench:
```
[bench] seq=64 batch=8 kv_warm=true
p50=42ms p95=118ms p99=240ms
mode mixed(fp8/int4) calib=on
note: spikes correlate with layer 18/19 calls
```

paul: layer 18/19 are attention-proj for this model, high KV reads. mixing kernels there might force extra memcpy or fallback to FP path for KV ops.

alex: hmm if kernel_selector switches kernels mid-run we might be incurring a penalty: kernel launch + dtype conversion for KV reads. Did you try excluding the attention layers from quantization instead?

maya: not yet. initial idea was exclude only embed+lm_head to keep logits quality. i can try exclude attention proj as well.

perf-bot: Automated note: Canary run 1938200025 triggered regression alert: tail_latency_delta=+14% vs baseline(1901122334). See /perf/runs/1938200025 for traces.

sam: perf-bot link looks useful. two things to test: 1) run same config but `--calib=off` to measure calibration overhead separately, 2) try `--batch=1` to see if batching masks the kernel-switch cost.

maya: ran both quickly: calib=off -> p95 back to ~102ms (so ~14ms saved). batch=1 -> p95 ~96ms (smaller p50 diff but p99 still high).

rachel: that suggests both calibration and batch-aggregation interact. calibration probably inserts dtype-copy ops into weight tensors and warms caches differently. batch=1 reducing batching means fewer kernel switches per micro-batch?

paul: another angle: KV cache layout differs for quantized layers. If we quantize keys/values to int4, reads need dequant on the hot path. maybe our runtime does dequant per token rather than per-block. expensive.

alex: can you dump a microtrace around the spike? I want to see if we have repeated dequant calls for the same KV chunk.

maya: here's excerpt from microtrace around 0.82s spike:
```
[0.815s] layer18_attention_kv_read -> int4_dequant (3.1ms)
[0.818s] layer18_attention_matmul -> fp8_kernel (1.2ms)
[0.821s] layer18_attention_kv_read -> int4_dequant (3.0ms)
```

sam: looks like duplicated dequant for same seq positions. that's a bug in the KV read cache dedupe. could be our cache key includes quantization state, so on switch we re-populate.

rachel: interesting — maybe calibration changes the quant params (scale/zero) and we don't reuse existing cached dequantized shards. two fixes: 1) make cache key ignore runtime quant params for reads, 2) perform dequant lazily per cached block only once.

paul: also re-check the kernel_scheduler heuristics: if it prioritizes fp8 kernels for matmul but int4 for kvaload, we may be ping-ponging between kernel contexts which hits driver warmup. we can bias scheduler to co-locate compatible kernels.

maya: next steps I'm doing: a) reproduce with attention excluded, b) run calib=off full bench, c) add a small patch to make KV cache key independent of quant params. will post results.

alex: for (c) watch out for correctness — if quant scale changes drastically between calib runs we might return wrong dequantized values. add a fast check: compare stored scale vs current, and if close (within 1e-3) allow reuse.

maya: good call. I'll do that threshold. also will add a short unit test for KV dedupe.

perf-bot: Note: create PR check required for KV cache changes: run 5k synthetic tokens validation and compare logits to baseline.

maya: created PR 4278 with KV cache key patch + unit test. bench results (quick): exclude attention -> p95 95ms, p99 170ms. calib=off -> p95 99ms. both patches combined -> p95 88ms, p99 150ms.

sam: nice improvement. can you also snapshot token quality (perplexity or a short eval set) to ensure excluding attention doesn't regress?

maya: ran eval on tiny devset: delta perplexity +0.002 for exclude-attn, +0.001 for our cache-key patch (within noise).

alex: sounds good. next: roll to canary for a day with autoscale on, and monitor cost delta (int4/FP8 tradeoff). rachel, paul — want to review the KV cache change before merge?

rachel: I'll take a look tonight. quick glance seems sane.

paul: me too. add a comment about kernel_scheduler heuristics; we should follow-up with a separate perf story to co-locate kernels.

maya: thanks all. will post final numbers in the perf dashboard and link here after 24h canary. :thumbsup:

alex: great work.
